sources.entry: justhtml - A pure Python HTML5 parser that sanitizes untrusted HTML by default.

summary.one_liner: JustHTML is a pure-Python, zero-dependency HTML5 parser that sanitizes untrusted HTML by default and offers CSS selector queries, transforms, text extraction, and Markdown output.
summary.what_it_does: It parses HTML the way a browser does, including recovering from malformed markup, and builds a single DOM. Sanitization is on by default using an allowlist, with URL policies and inline CSS controls, and can be turned off with sanitize=False for trusted input. Once parsed, you can query nodes with query() and query_one() using CSS selectors, and apply transforms such as Unwrap, Linkify, SetAttrs, and Drop. The DOM can be serialized back to HTML, converted to text with to_text(), or converted to Markdown. The package also includes a command-line tool for pretty-printing, selecting nodes, and extracting text or Markdown, plus a builder API and streaming for large inputs.
use_cases: parse broken or scraped web pages
query HTML with CSS selectors in Python
how_to_run: from justhtml import JustHTML; doc = JustHTML(html, fragment=True)
notable: Sanitizes by default: JustHTML(html) cleans output before querying or serializing
Zero runtime dependencies, no C extension, works on PyPy and Pyodide
Tested against the web platform html5 treebuilder tests with 100% line and branch coverage claimed
Transform pipeline (Unwrap, Drop, SetAttrs, Linkify) on a single parsed DOM
Bleach migration guide for moving existing sanitizer policies
caveats: The README says parsing terabytes of trusted HTML is better done with a C/Rust parser, since it is pure Python
Output is not automatically safe inside JavaScript, CSS, URL attributes, or other non-body contexts
